newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan airline to keep money losing SAfrican route.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan airline to keep money losing SAfrican route.

text.p: Taiwan's China Airlines acknowledged on Tuesday that it was losing money on its weekly Taipei-Johannesburg flight, but denied a local newspaper report that it would suspend the route.
"Frankly speaking, the route between Taiwan and South Africa has no economic efficiency. We have lost money from this operation," airline spokesman Steve Yang said.
"But we have no immediate intention to suspend the operation. We intend to continue for the time being," he said.
The decision had nothing to do with politics, he added.
The China Times Express newspaper said China Airlines was considering suspending the financially untenable route.
Taiwan Vice-Premier Hsu Li-teh is in South Africa, the island's largest diplomatic ally, for a nine-day visit.

Taiwan has diplomatic relations with only 30 countries. The rest of the world recognises rival Beijing, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province and refuses relations with any country that has official ties with Taiwan.
